summary: Checks whether a value is **not** object-like.
description: `nonObjectLike(value)` is the same test as `!isObjectLike(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
Everything `isObject` accepts, plus functions: the question it answers is whether properties can be read off the value at all.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not object-like; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonObjectLike(null); // => true
nonObjectLike("abc"); // => true
nonObjectLike(1); // => true
nonObjectLike({}); // => false
nonObjectLike([]); // => false
nonObjectLike(function () {}); // => false
```
